newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends higher, but interest remains thin.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends higher, but interest remains thin.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures posted strong gains on Friday, boosted by local and light speculative buying, traders said.
But turnover remained relatively modest, at an estimated 5,213 lots.
""There's really very little going on," said one trader. "There's no interest, it's very uninspiring."
The benchmark September contract reached a high of 167.00 cents per lb, but a late round of weekend profit-taking and steady origin selling trimmed gains, traders said.

By the close, September stood at 164.30 cents, up 3.85 cents on the day. Spot July, which expires on Monday, ended 5.60 cents higher, at 192.50 cents, while the outer months closed up 2.60 to down 0.30.
Coffee prices briefly softened at the outset, but dealers said trade buying below 160.00 in September stemmed losses and prompted some speculative short-covering at the reopening.
Upward momentum accelerated after September breached chart resistance at 163.00 and 165.00-166.00 cents, touching off light commission house buy-stops.

Trade interest in the switches also buoyed the market, with July/September widening to 28.20 cents compared with 26.45 cents at the close on Thursday and September/December stretching to 12.85 cents from 14.20 cents.
Dealers said there was some buying today on concerns that Hurricane Danny could potentially damage coffee stowed in New Orleans warehouses or disrupt coffee shipments to New Orleans.
"There is a hurricane in New Orleans and some people were afraid it could hit warehouses," said one trader. "Dampened coffee is problematic, it becomes moldy.
Danny, a minimal hurricane, swept across the tip of Lousiana on Friday, but its impact in New Orleans was limited to occasional showers and wind gusts.

Technically, traders pegged September resistance at 167.00-168.00 cents, with the next level seen near 170.00. Buy-stops were said to be building around 175.00. On the downside, support was put at 160.00.
After Friday's close, CSCE reported that certified coffee inventories rose by 3,441 60-kg bags as of July 17, to 80,592 bags. An additional 11,479 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
CSCE also reported that 31,787 bags of coffee were graded and only 8,478 bags had passed exchange approval.
